issue: Sequence-vs-slot conflation. The caption says 'each row is one sequence (slot) evolving over time', the legend calls pink an 'idle slot (bubble)', and the note says 'GPU slots idle (pink)'. If rows are sequences, the pink is per-sequence dead time, not slot occupancy; the bubble in discrete batching is a slot-level (column) property — the slot is occupied by the batch but under-filled. A reader can plausibly conclude the wrong thing about what is wasted.
evidence: Rendered p.200: legend 'idle slot (bubble)'; caption 'each row is one sequence (slot) evolving over time'; note 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. The horizontal axis is labelled 'time (decode steps / iterations)', so rows cannot simultaneously be slots.
acceptance_test: State the semantics unambiguously in one sentence, e.g. 'rows are sequences; pink marks slot time during which this sequence has already finished but the batch has not', and change the legend entry to 'slot time with this sequence finished (bubble)'. Alternatively redraw the bubble as a column-wise gap so slot occupancy is visible.

issue: The annotation 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' points at a green block, which is the new sequence, not the finishing sequence or the freed slot. The arrow therefore points to the wrong object.
evidence: Rendered figure: the arrow from that text terminates on a green block. The green block is the backfill sequence; the finishing sequence is the preceding blue block.
acceptance_test: Move the arrow to the boundary between the finishing blue block and the green backfill block, or relabel the annotation to 'a freed slot is refilled immediately'.

issue: The caption contains an out-of-context term: 'so short outputs idle in the training slots'. This is an inference figure; 'training slots' is wrong and will be read as a reference to training-time batching.
evidence: Rendered p.200 caption: 'In the left (discrete) panel a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in the training slots; in the right (continuous) panel freed slots are refilled every step.'
acceptance_test: Replace 'the training slots' with 'the idle slots' (or 'the slot'), and grep the manuscript for other occurrences of 'training' inside inference-serving captions.

issue: The 'next batch waits' annotation is a gray box with an arrow pointing to a row, not to the batch-completion boundary. It is visually ambiguous whether the next batch waits for that row, for the whole batch, or for the end of the time axis.
evidence: Left panel: gray box labeled 'next batch waits' sits below the rows with an upward arrow to the bottom row. The caption says 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes', which is a batch-wide condition, not a single-row condition.
acceptance_test: Replace the box-and-arrow with a bracket spanning the full batch duration and label it 'next batch cannot start until the slowest sequence finishes'; or otherwise anchor the annotation to the rightmost batch-completion edge.

issue: The backfill mechanism - the whole point of the right-hand panel - is drawn as hairline-thin green slivers (a few pixels wide at 150 dpi) and the accompanying annotation is set in green text on white, which is the lowest-contrast element on the page. At print size the reader may not see the green segments at all, and the annotation 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots' cannot be verified against the drawing.
evidence: Rendered p.200 continuous panel: green vertical slivers between/adjacent to blue blocks, one of which is the target of the annotation arrow; the annotation text itself is green.
acceptance_test: Inspect a 300 dpi crop of the continuous panel at 100% print size and confirm each green backfill segment is at least ~1.5 mm wide and clearly distinguishable from the adjacent blue block in grayscale; if not, widen the segments and set the annotation in black with a green leader.

issue: Blue and green are both solid fills and are distinguished only by color; the caption also uses color names ('green', 'pink') as load-bearing descriptors. In grayscale the blue/green distinction is not reliably recoverable.
evidence: Legend icons: blue solid square, green solid square. The diagram uses solid blue and solid green blocks with no pattern or in-block label. Caption: 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots' and 'GPU slots idle (pink)'.
acceptance_test: Add a hatch, outline, or small 'new' label to green blocks (or otherwise make the distinction pattern-based), and add a grayscale note; verify the figure remains interpretable in a grayscale print proof.

issue: The 'next batch waits' callout's arrow points upward into the bottom row's pink region rather than at the gap between one batch's completion and the next batch's start, so the callout's referent is ambiguous - it appears to point at idle time rather than at the blocked arrival.
evidence: Rendered p.200: grey box 'next batch waits' with the sub-label 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early', and a short upward arrow whose head lands on the lower edge of the fourth discrete row.
acceptance_test: Re-anchor the arrow so its head lands in the inter-batch gap (or on the left edge of the panel where the waiting request would queue), and confirm the arrowhead is unambiguous at print size.

issue: A cell in the 'Primary resource traded' column is garbled: the Continuous batching row reads 'compute-bound-width until'. This is not a meaningful phrase and appears to be a lost arrow or a lost word (presumably 'compute-bound -> bandwidth-bound until ...').
evidence: Rendered p.201, Table 11-1, row 'Continuous batching (Orca)': Mechanism 'Admit/evict at each decode step'; Primary resource traded 'compute-bound-width until'; When it matters 'high concurrency'; Source '[S1][1P]'.
acceptance_test: Replace the cell with a well-formed phrase (e.g. 'compute-bound -> bandwidth-bound until the batch fills'), and confirm the cell no longer wraps mid-token across two lines.

issue: The Discrete batching row's 'Primary resource traded' cell reads '— (wastes)', which is incomplete: it names no resource that is wasted. The em-dash plus parenthetical is also inconsistent with the column's other entries, which name a resource.
evidence: Rendered p.201, Table 11-1, row 'Discrete batching': Mechanism 'Lock batch to completion'; Primary resource traded '— (wastes)'; When it matters 'baseline only'; Source '—'.
acceptance_test: Either complete the cell (e.g. 'slot occupancy (wastes capacity)') or replace it with a consistent 'none' and move the waste statement into the 'When it matters' column.

issue: Table completeness is unverified: the table ends at the bottom of p.181 with the Prefix caching row and no continuation marker, while the chapter's own prose and the Fig. 11.2 caption name additional techniques (P/D disaggregation, chunked prefill, speculative decoding, KV quantization/offloading). If the table does not continue on p.182, the 'at a glance' table omits the chapter's headline technique.
evidence: Rendered p.201: Table 11-1 rows visible are Discrete batching, Continuous batching (Orca), PagedAttention / vLLM, Prefix caching (RadixAttention/APC); the page ends with whitespace below the table and no '(continued)' header. p.181 prose: 'P/D disaggregation (Splitwise/DistServe/Mooncake) is the architecture of choice'.
acceptance_test: Inspect p.182 and confirm the table continues with a repeated header and includes rows for chunked prefill, speculative decoding, and P/D disaggregation; if it does not, add them so the table matches the chapter's scope.

issue: The title says 'orthogonal concerns', but the caption immediately says the concerns interact ('batching pressure feeds KV residency') and that they are 'separable', not orthogonal. 'Orthogonal' is a stronger and contradictory claim.
evidence: Title: 'Serving = four orthogonal concerns, not a stack'. Caption: 'Serving is four separable concerns, not a stack (they interact — batching pressure feeds KV residency — but each is chosen independently)'.
acceptance_test: Change the title to 'four separable concerns' (or 'four concerns, not a stack') and remove 'orthogonal' unless the figure actually shows independence; keep 'separable but coupled' language consistent.

figure: FIGURE 11.2 (Serving = four orthogonal concerns, not a stack)
issue: The caption relies on an ordering the figure does not encode: 'the canonical baseline uses the first three; resource specialization joins when the workload outgrows a node'. In a 2x2 grid, 'the first three' depends entirely on an assumed reading order, and nothing marks RESOURCE SPECIALIZATION as the later addition. A reader can equally read the four boxes as a symmetric set with no baseline.
evidence: Rendered p.204: 2x2 grid, top row 'REQUEST SCHEDULING' (purple) / 'STATE MANAGEMENT' (red), bottom row 'REUSE' (green) / 'RESOURCE SPECIALIZATION' (orange); caption: 'the canonical baseline uses the first three; resource specialization joins when the workload outgrows a node (S11.3.6)'.
acceptance_test: Number the boxes 1-4 in the figure (or mark the fourth with a dashed border plus 'added when the workload outgrows a node') so the caption's 'first three' resolves without guessing the reading order.

issue: The caption claims 'a system can combine any mechanism with any other'. This is an unqualified universal claim; implementation support and resource interactions can prevent arbitrary combinations.
evidence: Caption: 'The four are independent dials — a system can combine any mechanism with any other'. The same caption admits interactions and the book elsewhere discusses implementation-dependent feature support.
acceptance_test: Soften to 'can be combined in principle, subject to implementation support and resource interactions' and add one concrete example of a combination that requires care.

figure: FIGURE 11.2 (Serving = four orthogonal concerns, not a stack)
issue: The figure is a four-label grid with no mechanism content, so it explains less than its caption does; the mapping from each concern to its concrete mechanism (Orca-style batching, PagedAttention, prefix caching, P/D disaggregation) exists only in caption prose. The figure also occupies a small fraction of the page with large surrounding whitespace, so the page's information density is low.
evidence: Rendered p.204: four large empty rounded rectangles containing only a two-line uppercase label; caption supplies the mechanisms in parentheses.
acceptance_test: Add one short mechanism exemplar inside each box (e.g. 'REQUEST SCHEDULING - continuous batching, chunked prefill') so the figure carries the mapping, and/or enlarge the boxes to use the available width.

figure: FIGURE 11.2 (Serving = four orthogonal concerns, not a stack)
issue: In grayscale the purple and orange box fills are close in luminance, so the four boxes are not cleanly separable by fill alone. The uppercase labels do carry the meaning, so this is cosmetic rather than semantic, but the figure relies on colour for visual grouping.
evidence: Rendered p.204: purple (#7x4xBF-like) and orange fills convert to similar mid-grays; red and green convert to distinguishable but also similar mid-grays.
acceptance_test: Check a grayscale proof of p.204; if the four fills are not separable, differentiate them by border weight or pattern so the grouping survives monochrome printing.

figure: Figure 11.3 — P/D disaggregation: two cases, two different KV links
issue: Panel A labels the link 'KV 450 GB/s' without the 'per direction' qualifier used in the prose. A reader can interpret 450 GB/s as aggregate bidirectional bandwidth rather than one-way transfer bandwidth.
evidence: Panel A: 'KV 450 GB/s'. Printed p. 184 prose: 'at NVLink's 450 GB/s per direction (§9.2) that transfer is 35 ÷ 450 ≈ 0.08 s'. The figure's arrow is one-way.
acceptance_test: Add 'per direction' to the panel A label or to the figure's link legend; confirm the caption and prose use the same qualifier.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 (P/D disaggregation: two cases, two different KV links)
issue: The caption's KV-transfer time contradicts the figure's own numbers by a factor of ~10. Caption: 'it moves the per-request KV state (~35 GB, 0.8 s) across the joining link'. Figure panel A: '~35 GB = 0.08 s (on-node)'; panel B: '~35 GB = 0.9 s (cross-host)'. The caption's '0.8 s' matches neither drawn value (it is 10x the on-node value and ~11% below the cross-host value).
evidence: Rendered p.205: panel A header '~35 GB = 0.08 s (on-node)'; panel B header '~35 GB = 0.9 s (cross-host)'; caption line 'it moves the per-request KV state (~35 GB, 0.8 s) across the joining link'. Independent recomputation: 35 GB / 450 GB/s = 0.0778 s -> 0.08 s (figure correct); 35 GB / 40 GB/s = 0.875 s -> 0.9 s (figure correct). The caption's 0.8 s is not derivable from either link rate.
acceptance_test: Caption and figure agree on both cases: caption reads '(~35 GB, 0.08 s on-node / 0.9 s cross-host)' or the figure is changed to match the caption. Verify by re-rendering p.205 and confirming that every KV time printed in the caption equals the corresponding drawn value.

figure: Figure 11.3 — P/D disaggregation: two cases, two different KV links
issue: The figure's caveat uses 40 req/s, while the surrounding canonical discussion uses ~10 rps. The figure does not state why 40 req/s is the relevant peak or that it is a different operating point.
evidence: Figure caveat: '35 GB/request × 40 req/s = 1.4 TB/s of payload.' Printed p. 181: 'For the canonical single-host (~10 rps) this disaggregation is premature'. The figure does not label 40 req/s as an illustrative peak.
acceptance_test: Label 40 req/s explicitly as an illustrative peak / outgrown-node operating point, or add a sentence in the caption explaining the relationship to the ~10 rps canonical baseline.
